findings.detail: The new block in scripts/test_shiki_init.sh runs `python3 scripts/validate_shiki.py`, full `unittest discover -s tests`, AND every shipped scripts/test_shiki_*.sh (23 scripts, each spinning up temp repos/subprocesses) inside the fresh target. Because test_shiki_init.sh is itself part of the task's test_command and is invoked by CI's shiki-validate.yml `for script in scripts/test_shiki_*.sh` loop, this materially increases wall-clock for both the loop's TDD gate and the required Validate check. It is bounded (one level of nesting; the nested test_shiki_init.sh skips the block via SHIKI_INIT_SKIP_INSTALL_VERIFY=1) and correct, but the same 10-minute command-timeout strand that motivated the session-lease work is a real exposure here. This is a runtime/robustness concern, not a correctness defect — flagging so an operator can watch for CI/dispatch timeouts.
findings.title: Install-and-verify runs the entire shipped contract suite inside a target, nested inside test_shiki_init.sh (heavy runtime, timeout-prone)

findings.detail: find_unshipped_dependencies treats the two TARGET_INSTALL_EXCLUDES test files (tests/test_loop_e2e_contract.py, tests/test_mirror_lock_injection.py) as shipped, because is_shipped() returns True for anything under the shipped `tests` directory. So if a shipped artifact ever depended on one of those explicitly-excluded files, the static check would NOT flag it even though the file never reaches a target. No such dependency exists today (they are leaf tests, depended on by nothing), so this is latent only. Worth a follow-up guard if the exclude list grows.
findings.title: Completeness check has a latent blind spot for TARGET_INSTALL_EXCLUDES files

scope:
Close the four measured gaps AND the class that produced them.

The four gaps: add `tests` and `.gitignore` to `TEMPLATE_PATHS`; add `scripts/shiki_session_lease.py` and `scripts/shiki_contract_approval.py` to `TEMPLATE_PATHS`; and stop copying `.shiki/leases` into a target — the natural fix is to register `.shiki/leases` in the manifest the same way the other runtime-local state directories are registered, so `should_skip` filters it for the same reason it already filters `.shiki/ledger` and `.shiki/gha`. Whatever mechanism is chosen, a lock file must never reach a target and must never be committable there.

The class: add `tests/test_install_completeness.py` with a STATIC check over the shipping surface. For every shipped Python module under `scripts/`, every shipped `scripts/test_shiki_*.sh`, and every shipped `.github/workflows/*.yml`, resolve the repository-relative artifacts it depends on — Python imports of sibling `shiki_*` modules, `scripts/...` and `tests/...` paths referenced in shell and YAML, and the directory a `unittest discover -s <dir>` names — and assert each is either in `TEMPLATE_PATHS` or on an EXPLICIT, commented exception list. The exception list must be a named constant with a reason per entry, so an omission is a deliberate recorded decision rather than an oversight. This is the check that would have caught all four gaps at once.

Add an install-and-verify case to `scripts/test_shiki_init.sh`: install into a fresh temporary directory, then, from inside that directory, run the target's own `python3 scripts/validate_shiki.py`, `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests`, and every shipped `scripts/test_shiki_*.sh`, asserting zero failures. Assert also that `.shiki/leases` is absent or empty in the installed target and that the installed `.gitignore` ignores it. This test is the acceptance for the whole task: if a fresh install cannot pass its own required checks, it fails.

REPRODUCIBILITY — what this task removes, and what to change to get the same result.
  Symptom: `shiki init` prints `target Shiki validation passed` and exits 0. The operator now has a repository whose every PR is permanently red on `Validate Shiki mirror` — and because `init` also applied branch protection requiring that check, nothing in that repository can ever merge.
  Measured 2026-08-03 against main at 93cf467: `TEMPLATE_PATHS` has 77 entries. `'tests' in TEMPLATE_PATHS` -> False, while the shipped `.github/workflows/shiki-validate.yml:31` runs `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests`. `'scripts/shiki_session_lease.py' in TEMPLATE_PATHS` -> False, while the shipped `scripts/test_shiki_runner_claude.sh` imports that module. `'scripts/shiki_contract_approval.py' in TEMPLATE_PATHS` -> False, while the shipped `scripts/test_shiki_guardian_policy.sh` asserts its behaviour. `'.gitignore' in TEMPLATE_PATHS` -> False.
  Fourth cause, measured by calling the installer's own filter: `should_skip(ROOT/'.shiki/leases/x.lock', target_install=True)` -> False, versus True for `.shiki/ledger/L-1.json` and `.shiki/gha/pr.json`. The mirror directories are filtered because they appear in the manifest's `create_directories` list; `.shiki/leases` does not appear there. The platform's live lock — naming a task id from another repository — is therefore copied in, and with no `.gitignore` shipped it is committed.
  Why a static completeness check and not four additions: all four are the same defect — a shipped artifact depending on something unshipped, with nothing checking the relationship. Adding four paths fixes today and not tomorrow.
  Reproducible when: a fresh install passes its own validate, its own unittest discovery, and every shipped contract test, and the completeness check fails if any shipped artifact gains an unshipped dependency.
test_command: python3 -m unittest discover -s tests && bash scripts/test_shiki_init.sh && python3 scripts/validate_shiki.py --target .
title: Ship everything a shipped artifact depends on, and prove a fresh install works
